title: Markets: Monday 9 November

morning.session_note: Weekday ASX edition · before the 10:00 open
summary: Wall Street rose on Friday as chip stocks bounced after Thursday's sharp AI-led fall, but the S&P 500 still fell 2.7% on the week and Japan's market fell more than 9%; the ASX 200 closed Friday at 9,020.8 (−0.5%) and ABC reported futures pointing to a 0.2% higher open ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/asx-markets-business-live-news/107361534), [SMH](https://www.smh.com.au/business/markets/asx-eyes-gains-wall-street-steadies-as-ai-stocks-rebound-20261109-p61cfz.html)).

For Australia: the RBA cash rate is 4.85% after a 6–3 vote on 3 November and the Australian dollar closed Friday at US$0.6900 (−1.63%). ANZ reported a full-year cash profit of A$7.59 billion this morning ([ANZ](https://www.anz.com.au/newsroom/media/2026/november/2026-full-year-result%2D%2D%2Dproposed-final-dividend/)), and RBA Assistant Governor (Economic) Sarah Hunter speaks at 9:30am ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/media/)).

Next catalyst: US October CPI, due 12:30am Wednesday Sydney time (8:30am Tuesday in New York); futures pricing implies about an 80% chance of a Fed rate rise on 9 December ([BLS](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/cpi.htm), [LSEG data via Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/as-tech-swoon-roils-market-us-inflation-data-on-tap-5007256)).

cards.headline: Chips rebound Friday after Thursday's AI-led sell-off; week still lower
cards.takeaway: US stocks recovered part of Thursday's fall on Friday, and investors are still weighing how Democratic control of Congress could affect AI and data-centre spending.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday and Sunday issues carried Friday's close. New today: ABC's weekly tally (S&P 500 −2.7%, Philadelphia Semiconductor Index +4.2% Friday), Fox Business and Reuters detail on the policy debate behind the selloff, and Asian reaction.
cards.what_happened: Wall Street rose on Friday as buyers returned to chip stocks. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 4.2% after Thursday's 12.2% fall, and Nvidia rose nearly 3%; the Dow fell 0.5% ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/asx-markets-business-live-news/107361534), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)). Thursday was the worst day for the three main US indexes since April 2025: the Nasdaq fell 5.5% and the S&P 500 4.4%, on worries that Democratic wins in the 3 November midterms could slow AI and data-centre building ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/stock-market-today-live-updates.html), [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/trump-blames-democrats-stock-market-plunge-after-sweeping-midterm-victories)). President Trump wrote on Truth Social that the market fall was "based on the results of the Election" and that "Your 401(k)s have, therefore, dropped"; on Friday he said he is 100% in favour of the AI build-out. Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, a Democrat, said in a CNN interview that Texas should "stop what we are doing with data centers until we have measures to protect Texans" ([Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/trump-blames-democrats-stock-market-plunge-after-sweeping-midterm-victories), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)). Democrats won majorities in both chambers of Congress and will hold them from 2027; Trump retains the veto ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/as-tech-swoon-roils-market-us-inflation-data-on-tap-5007256), [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/new-political-landscape-facing-ai-after-democrats-midterm-gains)).
cards.why_it_matters: FNArena describes the ASX as having considerably lower AI exposure than US markets, but a US growth scare would feed into US rates and the Australian dollar, and copper fell to its lowest since July on data-centre rollout worries (ABC). Analysts disagree on how large the policy effect will be (views below).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard (6 Nov close): S&P 500 7,376.9 (+0.3%), Nasdaq 24,579.4 (+1.1%), VIX 25.64 (−2.54 pts). ABC reported the S&P 500 down 2.7% on the week; copper fell to its lowest since July on data-centre rollout worries.

competing_views.who: State Street Investment Management strategists (Elliot Hentov, Christine Norton)
competing_views.view: Said Democratic gains could add headwinds for AI providers and data-centre development, but that Congress alone could not curtail construction in the face of a presidential veto, and that AI investment will likely stay robust in 2027, tempered by supply-chain strain and tighter credit.

Said data-centre pauses in states such as Texas put about 30% of expected 2028 additions at risk, a negative for semiconductors and AI infrastructure, while noting semiconductor valuations are near multi-year lows and positioning has been cut sharply.
Told Reuters most of the disruption to the AI buildout will probably not occur, and that the uncertainty comes from the change in control at federal, state and local levels.

cards.what_to_watch: CoreWeave, Applied Materials and Cisco earnings this week, and whether chips hold Friday's bounce after US CPI.

cards.headline: Asian chip stocks fell sharply Friday; Japan's market down over 9% on the week
cards.takeaway: Asia absorbed Thursday's Nasdaq fall before Wall Street's Friday bounce, with Japan and Korea hit hardest and China's shares up on the week.
cards.key_figure: Japan's market −9%+ on the week; China shares +1.7%; ASX 200 +1.3% (ABC, week to 6 Nov)
cards.what_happened: Asian technology stocks fell on Friday after the Nasdaq's Thursday drop: SK Hynix −10.44%, Samsung Electronics −6.35%, SoftBank Group −10.83% and TSMC −4.69%, while Tokyo and Seoul indexes each fell about 6% ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/tech-stocks-sk-hynix-samsung-softbank.html), [SMH](https://www.smh.com.au/business/markets/asx-eyes-gains-wall-street-steadies-as-ai-stocks-rebound-20261109-p61cfz.html)). ABC's weekly tally had Japan down more than 9%, China up 1.7%, Europe up 0.6% and the ASX up 1.3% ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/asx-markets-business-live-news/107361534)). Goldman Sachs's Timothy Moe said position unwinding and stop-loss selling worsened the fall and that political opposition to US data-centre building could affect Asian hardware suppliers ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/tech-stocks-sk-hynix-samsung-softbank.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: The ASX finished the week 1.3% higher while Tokyo and Seoul fell sharply; FNArena attributes Australia's relative resilience to its considerably lower AI exposure. The first Asian sessions this week will show whether Friday's US bounce carries into chip-heavy markets.
cards.market_reaction: ASX 200 closed Friday 9,020.8 (−0.5%) in the dashboard. Asian index moves are as reported by CNBC, SMH and ABC; they are not in our snapshot.
cards.what_to_watch: Monday open in Tokyo and Seoul; SoftBank and SK Hynix after Friday's falls.

cards.headline: Brent flat near US$98 as Iran and the US restate positions; Qatari mediation continues
cards.takeaway: Brent was flat on Friday after a 17% weekly fall, the largest percentage fall since the start of the COVID pandemic (ABC); reported mine incidents, strike warnings and mediation leave the Hormuz outlook unresolved.
cards.key_figure: Brent futures US$98.32 (flat, 6 Nov); Brent spot US$107.03 as at 3 Nov (lagged series)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday and Sunday covered the Qeshm strikes and the Qatar plan. New on Sunday: Iran's foreign minister said the "2-day proposal stands" and warned of retaliation if US attacks resume; Trump said renewed strikes were "highly unlikely" if talks progress; Iranian state media reported two more tankers hit mines. New today: Iraq's foreign minister said Iraq has reached understandings with the US on exports through Hormuz.
cards.what_happened: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that Iran's "2-day proposal stands" and that if the US resumes attacks Iran will "rain down hell"; Trump said in a phone interview that renewed strikes were "highly unlikely" if talks on the nuclear programme and Hormuz progress, adding that three US aircraft carriers were ready to strike if necessary ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8/iran-threatens-to-rain-down-hell-if-us-escalates-war)). Iran's military said two tankers caught fire after hitting mines on an "unauthorised route", and US Central Command said it disabled a ship that tried to breach the US blockade ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-08/iran-strait-of-hormuz-update-explosions-talks/107360730)). Similar Iranian claims earlier this year were not independently confirmed, and CENTCOM said in August that it had cleared mines from the established shipping lanes, a statement shipping groups met with scepticism at the time ([The Daily Energy](https://thedailyenergy.com/iran-tankers-mines-hormuz-november4/)). Iran is reviewing Qatari proposals on its nuclear programme, but an official told AP Iran remains unwilling to negotiate on it until the US agrees to several conditions ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-08/iran-strait-of-hormuz-update-explosions-talks/107360730)). Iraq's foreign minister Fuad Hussein told Al Jazeera that Iraq has reached understandings with the US to allow Iraqi oil exports through Hormuz via a lane near Oman ([ABC, citing Reuters](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/asx-markets-business-live-news/107361534)). Brent futures were flat at US$98.32 on Friday after falling about 17% on the week ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/asx-markets-business-live-news/107361534)).
cards.why_it_matters: Fuel prices feed into Australian inflation: RBA Governor Michele Bullock said on 3 November that global oil prices are part of the reason inflation is expected to stay higher for longer, but that the rate rise addresses domestic capacity pressures rather than oil directly ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/mc-gov-2026-11-03.html)). Energy stocks fell nearly 8% on the ASX last week as oil dropped ([FNArena](https://fnarena.com/2026/11/06/next-week-at-a-glance-9-13-nov-2026/)).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: Brent futures 98.32 (flat, 6 Nov session); gold futures 4,074.9 (−0.9%). Brent spot 107.03 is a lagged official series as at 3 Nov. Iron ore is unavailable in our snapshot; ABC reported it at US$92.40/t on Friday (−0.7%).
cards.priced_in: Brent settled at US$98.29 on Thursday 5 Nov, up 3.9% after tumbling more than 8% on Wednesday to its lowest settlement since 31 August, according to Reuters.

competing_views.view: Said in a note that any escalation could push Brent into a US$110–125 range.
Said Brent's drop to near US$93 was arguably too optimistic, and that it has since traded back above US$99.

FRED's series is Brent spot as published by the EIA with a lag, last at 3 November, when the futures price was higher than it is now. They measure different instruments on different dates, so both are shown and not averaged.

cards.what_to_watch: Any published text from Qatari mediation, UKMTO incident reports, further mine incidents in the strait, and OPEC's monthly report this week.

cards.headline: ANZ reports A$7.59bn full-year cash profit; ASX futures point to a small gain
cards.takeaway: ANZ's cash profit was slightly above the A$7.5bn consensus ABC cited, and its full-year dividend of A$1.66 was below the A$1.70 expected; ASX 200 futures were about 0.2% higher after Friday's 0.5% fall.
cards.key_figure: ANZ FY26 cash profit A$7,591m (+31%; +10% excluding FY25 significant items), final dividend 83c, full year 166c; ASX 200 9,020.8 (−0.5%, 6 Nov close)
cards.new_since_last_issue: ANZ's result was released this morning; the weekend issue listed it as scheduled. Futures levels are from ABC and SMH because our own SPI feed is unavailable.
cards.what_happened: ANZ announced a full-year statutory profit of A$7,270 million and a cash profit of A$7,591 million. Cash profit was up 31% on the prior year, or up 10% excluding FY25 significant items; the final dividend is 83 cents (80% franked), taking the full-year dividend to 166 cents, and CET1 capital was 11.99%. The credit impairment charge for the year was A$582 million ([ANZ](https://www.anz.com.au/newsroom/media/2026/november/2026-full-year-result%2D%2D%2Dproposed-final-dividend/)). ABC listed the consensus as a cash profit of about A$7.5 billion and a dividend of A$1.70 a share against A$1.66 last year, and described the profit as slightly ahead of expectations and the dividend as slightly lower ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/asx-markets-business-live-news/107361534)). ASX 200 futures pointed to a gain of about 22 points, or 0.2%, at 9,036, after the index closed Friday at 9,021 (−0.5%) and finished the week 1.3% higher ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/asx-markets-business-live-news/107361534), [SMH](https://www.smh.com.au/business/markets/asx-eyes-gains-wall-street-steadies-as-ai-stocks-rebound-20261109-p61cfz.html)). Last week's bank results were mixed: FNArena said Westpac slightly disappointed, NAB missed by more as bad-debt provisioning rose, and Macquarie beat expectations ([FNArena](https://fnarena.com/2026/11/06/next-week-at-a-glance-9-13-nov-2026/)).
cards.why_it_matters: ANZ's profit, credit charge and dividend are one reading of how higher rates are flowing through bank earnings, following mixed results from Westpac, NAB and Macquarie last week.
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: ASX 200 9,020.8 (−0.5%, 6 Nov). SPI 200 futures are unavailable in our feed; ABC reported futures +0.2% to 9,036 and the Australian dollar at about US68.67¢ at 6:47am. ANZ's share-price reaction at the 10:00am open is not available at the time of writing.
cards.what_to_watch: ANZ shares at the open against the result, and the CBA and Bendigo quarterly updates this week.

cards.headline: NextDC rose about 51% after Goodman and Digital Realty bought a stake
cards.takeaway: Goodman Group and Digital Realty bought a stake in NextDC through an aftermarket bookbuild at A$9.50; NextDC closed 50.84% higher on Thursday while US data-centre stocks fell.
cards.key_figure: NextDC +50.84% on 5 Nov; ASX Info Tech index about +8% for the week (FNArena)
cards.what_happened: Goodman Group and Digital Realty ran an aftermarket bookbuild on 4 November seeking up to 9.9% of NextDC at A$9.50 a share; NextDC's board called the move "opportunistic" and noted it came two weeks after a power-supply delay at its M3 Melbourne site and a revision to FY27 guidance. The buyers told investors they have no current intention of making a takeover bid but reserved the right to do so, and NextDC said it holds no takeover proposal ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/nextdc-goodman-group-digital-realty-data-centers-.html), [NextDC statement](https://www.eqs-news.com/news/inside-information-ad-hoc-release/nextdc-limited-response-to-share-raid-by-goodman-group-and-digital-realty/32a0ca02-6283-42ef-888d-fc9568fbf2ec_en)). The AFR reported the pair acquired just under 8%, with their joint stake not yet confirmed ([AFR](https://www.afr.com/street-talk/goodman-digital-realty-grab-7-5pc-of-nextdc-in-aftermarket-raid-20261105-p61bkw)). FNArena said NextDC's rally lifted the Info Tech index about 8% for the week ([FNArena](https://fnarena.com/2026/11/06/next-week-at-a-glance-9-13-nov-2026/)).
cards.why_it_matters: NextDC rose in the same week US data-centre stocks fell. The RBA has said data-centre investment adds to demand in an economy that is already capacity constrained, while productivity gains have yet to show ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/mc-gov-2026-11-03.html)).
cards.what_to_watch: Any NextDC response to the stake, and substantial-holder notices from Goodman and Digital Realty.

cards.headline: Housing keeps falling as consumer sentiment and business surveys land Tuesday
cards.takeaway: Home prices fell a further 1.2% in October, and Morgan Stanley has joined CommBank in forecasting a 10–15% peak-to-trough fall; Westpac–Melbourne Institute sentiment is due Tuesday.
cards.key_figure: Cotality home prices −1.2% in October, 6.7% below March peak (Westpac); consumer sentiment last 80.4
cards.what_happened: Westpac said Cotality home prices fell a further 1.2% in October and are 6.7% below March's peak, and that household spending rose 0.6% in September but real volumes grew a more modest 0.7% in Q3 ([Westpac IQ weekly](https://library.westpaciq.com.au/content/dam/public/westpaciq/secure/economics/documents/aus/2026/11/WestpacWeekly20261109.pdf)). Westpac-Melbourne Institute consumer sentiment fell 4.7% to 80.4 in October, and Westpac said responses deteriorated sharply after the RBA's rate hike ([Westpac IQ weekly](https://library.westpaciq.com.au/content/dam/public/westpaciq/secure/economics/documents/aus/2026/11/WestpacWeekly20261109.pdf)). FNArena reported that Morgan Stanley has joined CommBank in forecasting a 10–15% peak-to-trough fall in residential property prices, with a bottom unlikely before the second half of 2027 ([FNArena](https://fnarena.com/2026/11/06/next-week-at-a-glance-9-13-nov-2026/)).
cards.why_it_matters: Governor Bullock said on 3 November that the housing market is responding to rate rises and that weaker turnover feeds into consumption ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/mc-gov-2026-11-03.html)). Tuesday's surveys will show how household and business confidence stand after the October hike.
cards.what_to_watch: Tuesday's Westpac-Melbourne Institute sentiment index (October 80.4) and NAB business conditions (September −1); Wednesday's Q3 housing finance approvals, where Westpac forecasts −10% against a −8.5% market forecast.

sources.label: Westpac IQ Australia and NZ Weekly

cards.headline: RBA at 4.85% after a 6–3 vote; chief economist speaks at 9:30am
cards.takeaway: Westpac and UBS both expect a December hold, and Governor Bullock said the Board is "preserving our options"; Sarah Hunter's speech is the first RBA commentary of the week.
cards.key_figure: RBA cash rate 4.85% (last move +25 bp, early November); AU 10-year yield 5.08% as at 4 Nov (RBA F2)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Today adds Sarah Hunter's speech (9:30am AEDT) and the AU 10-year comparison below; earlier issues covered the decision and Westpac's pause view.
cards.what_happened: The RBA raised the cash rate by 25 bp to 4.85% on 3 November in a 6–3 vote. Governor Bullock said the members favouring a hold weighed the downside risks more heavily, that after five rises it is "probably a good point to just take stock", and that she does not give forward guidance ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/mc-gov-2026-11-03.html), [Westpac IQ](https://www.westpaciq.com.au/economics/2026/11/rba-decision-3-november-2026)). The statement dropped September's wording on raising rates further "if needed" ([Westpac IQ](https://www.westpaciq.com.au/economics/2026/11/rba-decision-3-november-2026)). RBA Assistant Governor (Economic) Sarah Hunter speaks at the UBS Australasia Conference at 9:30am AEDT today ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/media/)). Background from before the decision: in a 60 Minutes interview broadcast on 25 October she said higher rates will bring inflation down and that oil-driven price pressure would get "a little bit" worse before it improves ([Kalkine](https://kalkine.com.au/news/economic-news/hauser-at-anu-hunter-at-ubs-baker-at-arca-the-rbas-post-cup-day-speaking-line-up)).
cards.why_it_matters: The RBA expects policy to work through mortgage and business lending; any change in tone from Ms Hunter on the December meeting could move bank shares, the Australian dollar and bond yields.
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: RBA cash rate 4.85%; AU 2-year 4.83% and 10-year 5.08% (RBA F2, as at 4 Nov); curve +26 bp. ABC reported the 10-year at 5.01% on Monday morning and Westpac at 5.02% on 6 November.

competing_views.view: Expects the RBA to hold in December and sees February as the next plausible hike timing, but only as a risk; calls November likely the peak of the cycle.
Expects the RBA to stay on hold at 4.85%, then cut twice in late 2027 and early 2028.
Said the Board is "preserving our options", and that the statement should not be read as saying rates are not going up or that they definitely are.

comparison.title: Which Australian 10-year yield?
comparison.why_different: The RBA's F2 series in our snapshot is lagged to 4 November. ABC and Westpac quote later market yields (9 November morning and 6 November). The gap most likely reflects timing and different data providers; the figures are shown side by side and not averaged.

rows.source: RBA F2 capital market yields, via our snapshot
rows.measure: Australian Government 10-year bond yield, official series
rows.method: Official series, published with a lag

cards.what_to_watch: Ms Hunter's remarks and Q&A (9:30am), Ms Baker's speech Thursday 12 November (10:30am AEDT), and the RBA minutes plus Governor Bullock's ASIC forum panel on 17 November.

cards.headline: Fed December hike odds near 80% after October payrolls beat forecasts
cards.takeaway: US payrolls beat forecasts and futures pricing for a 9 December rise moved to about 80%; October CPI arrives early Wednesday Sydney time.
cards.key_figure: US 10-year 4.86% (+2 bp), US 2-year 4.51% (+5 bp), 6 Nov close; October payrolls +165,000, unemployment 4.1%
cards.new_since_last_issue: Weekend issues cited CME FedWatch at 76.8% via 24/7 Wall St. New: Reuters/LSEG put pricing near 80%; CPI release time confirmed by BLS as 12:30am Wednesday AEDT (earlier issue said Tuesday evening).
cards.what_happened: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October and unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%; CNBC cited a Dow Jones consensus of 59,000 jobs, while ABC cited a consensus of 70,000 ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/stock-market-today-live-updates.html), [ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/asx-markets-business-live-news/107361534)). The Fed raised rates in September and held in October. After the jobs report, Fed funds futures were suggesting roughly an 80% chance of a hike at the 8–9 December meeting, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters, with about two more 25 bp rises expected this cycle ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/as-tech-swoon-roils-market-us-inflation-data-on-tap-5007256)). The Bureau of Labor Statistics will release October CPI on 10 November at 8:30am New York time, which is 12:30am Wednesday in Sydney ([BLS](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/cpi.htm)). Westpac's table shows a market forecast of +0.3% for the headline month versus +0.6% in September, and Westpac itself forecasts +0.4% headline and +0.2% core ([Westpac IQ weekly](https://library.westpaciq.com.au/content/dam/public/westpaciq/secure/economics/documents/aus/2026/11/WestpacWeekly20261109.pdf)).
cards.why_it_matters: Fed pricing moves US yields and the US dollar, which are inputs to the Australian dollar and to ASX rate-sensitive sectors. ABC attributed the Australian dollar's 2.3% weekly fall to strong US data, global risk aversion and a softer domestic growth outlook.
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: US 10-year 4.86% (+2 bp), US 2-year 4.51% (+5 bp), AUD/USD 0.6900 (−1.63%, RBA 4pm series, 6 Nov). ABC reported the Australian dollar at US68.67¢ on Monday morning.

competing_views.view: Said gaining enough comfort for the FOMC not to hike in December is a "high bar", and that the probability of further hikes in 2027 should continue to fall, particularly if Middle East tensions abate.
Said that if CPI is hot and inflation looks to be accelerating, additional tightening would be "something else that investors would have to absorb".

cards.what_to_watch: CPI at 12:30am Wednesday AEDT; Goolsbee speaks Monday US time; Fed speakers Hammack, Goolsbee and Daly later in the week.

cards.headline: Saudi Arabia says missiles intercepted over Riyadh; Aramco building damaged by debris
cards.takeaway: Saudi authorities said no one was hurt when falling debris damaged an Aramco administrative building; the Houthis said they carried out attacks on Saudi targets.
cards.what_happened: Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said an Aramco administrative building in Riyadh sustained minor damage from falling shrapnel in an "attempted" attack on Sunday, with no casualties; the Saudi-led coalition said its air defences destroyed two ballistic and two cruise missiles launched by Yemen's Houthis at Riyadh and other regions ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8/saudi-arabia-intercepts-houthi-missiles-targeting-riyadh-eastern-province), [AP](https://apnews.com/article/mideast-news-november-8-2026-090d96e25872f5c63e105b9dd3e5dc60)). Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group carried out four operations on Sunday, including strikes on Riyadh and on Aramco facilities in Abqaiq, and said they caused significant damage and fires; the Saudi side has not confirmed those claims ([The National](https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/gulf/2026/11/08/saudi-led-coalition-intercepts-two-houthi-missiles-fired-towards-riyadh/)). Al Jazeera said it could not independently verify casualty reports from either side in the wider Yemen fighting ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8/saudi-arabia-intercepts-houthi-missiles-targeting-riyadh-eastern-province)).
cards.why_it_matters: Houthi attacks on Saudi targets, including the Ras Tanura and Rabigh refineries, have escalated since a Yemen truce collapsed in July (Al Jazeera). This adds a supply-risk channel for oil that is separate from Hormuz.
cards.what_to_watch: Any damage to export infrastructure and Brent's reaction at Monday's open.

cards.headline: Australian dollar at lowest since March; gold up more than 5% on the week
cards.takeaway: The Australian dollar fell 2.3% last week, which ABC attributed to strong US data, global risk aversion and a softer domestic growth outlook, while gold rose more than 5% on the week despite slipping on Friday.
cards.key_figure: AUD/USD 0.6900 (−1.63%, 6 Nov); gold futures US$4,074.9 (−0.9%, 6 Nov)
cards.what_happened: ABC reported the Australian dollar fell 2.3% last week to its lowest since March on strong US data, global risk aversion and a softer domestic growth outlook, and traded around US68.67¢ on Monday morning (−0.9%) ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/asx-markets-business-live-news/107361534)). Gold slipped 0.1% on Friday, which ABC linked to higher rates and the stronger US dollar, but gained more than 5% for the week to close above US$4,000 an ounce ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-09/asx-markets-business-live-news/107361534)). Westpac's forecast table has AUD/USD at 0.72 by December 2026 ([Westpac IQ weekly](https://library.westpaciq.com.au/content/dam/public/westpaciq/secure/economics/documents/aus/2026/11/WestpacWeekly20261109.pdf)).
cards.why_it_matters: A lower Australian dollar raises import prices over time; Governor Bullock said on 3 November that import-price pass-through can take 9 to 12 months ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/mc-gov-2026-11-03.html)). Gold is quoted in US dollars, so it can also move with the US dollar and rate expectations.
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: AUD/USD 0.6900 (−1.63%, RBA 4pm series 6 Nov); gold futures 4,074.9 (−0.9%, 6 Nov). ABC's −0.9% and 68.67¢ are Monday-morning quotes against a different reference point, and its −0.1% gold figure is for spot gold, so these are not directly comparable with the dashboard.
cards.what_to_watch: US CPI and the US dollar; Chinese CPI and trade data this week.

forecasts.view: Expects the cash rate to be held in December; February is the next plausible hike timing, as a risk rather than a base case.
Expects the RBA to stay on hold at 4.85%, then cut twice in late 2027 and early 2028.

fed.summary: Fed funds futures suggested roughly an 80% chance of a quarter-point rise at the 8–9 December meeting, with about two more 25 bp rises expected in total for the cycle, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters.

forecasts.view: Said not hiking in December is a high bar, but further 2027 hikes should become less likely if Middle East tensions ease.
